newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler Q1 U.S. retail incentives rise.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler Q1 U.S. retail incentives rise.

text.p: Chrysler Corp said Thursday that its average U.S. retail incentive for the first quarter rose to $705 per vehicle from $640 a year ago and $660 in the 1996 fourth period.

By the end of the 1997 first quarter, the automaker said the average incentive had increased to $785 a vehicle. Although incentives were up, Chrysler officials said higher volume and higher prices on some of its profitable vehicles helped offset those costs.
Chrysler announced first quarter fully diluted net income of $1.45 a share, versus $1.30 a year ago.
Chrysler's after-tax profit per vehicle for the first quarter slipped to $1,198 from $1,200 a year ago, the company reported.
Worldwide factory unit shipments rose to 781,239 from 753,176 in the 1996 first period. In the 1996 fourth quarter, Chrysler shipped 753,326 units.
